subject: maths
title: Year 4 Fractions
seo_title: Year 4 Fractions Worksheets: Equivalent Fractions, Adding and Subtracting, Fractions of Amounts (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Recognise and show, using diagrams, families of common equivalent fractions; solve problems involving increasingly harder fractions to calculate quantities, and fractions to divide quantities, including non-unit fractions where the answer is a whole number; add and subtract fractions with the same denominator.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 fractions worksheets for the National Curriculum: equivalent fractions on a fraction wall, missing numbers, adding and subtracting with the same denominator, fractions of amounts and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Same denominator: add the numerators and keep the denominator. Fraction of an amount: divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator.
key_sub: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7, not 5/14. 3/4 of 24: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, then 6 × 3 = 18. Equivalent fractions: multiply the numerator and denominator by the same number, so 3/4 = 9/12.
body_html:
Numerator and denominator

The denominator (bottom number) tells you how many equal parts the whole is split into. The numerator (top number) tells you how many of those parts you have. In 34, the whole is split into 4 equal parts and we have 3 of them.

Equivalent fractions

Equivalent fractions are worth the same amount. A fraction wall shows them: look straight down to find fractions that line up.

To find an equivalent fraction, multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number.

Example

Find the missing number: 34 = ?12

4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the denominator by 3. Do the same to the numerator: 3 × 3 = 9.

Answer: 9

Fractions in one family are all equal: 13 = 26 = 39 = 412.

When the numerator is bigger than the denominator, the fraction is more than 1 whole. 54 is 4 quarters (1 whole) and 1 more quarter, so 54 = 1 14. This is a mixed number.

Adding and subtracting

When the denominators are the same, the parts are the same size. Add or subtract the numerators. Keep the denominator.

Example

910 − 410 = ?

Subtract the numerators: 9 − 4 = 5. The parts are still tenths.

Answer: 510

Example

35 + 45 = ?

3 + 4 = 7, so the total is 75. 55 is 1 whole, and 2 fifths are left over.

Answer: 1 25

Fractions of amounts

To find a fraction of an amount, divide by the denominator to find one part, then multiply by the numerator.

Example

What is 25 of £40?

£40 ÷ 5 = £8 for one fifth. Two fifths: £8 × 2 = £16.

Answer: £16

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the denominators: 27 + 37 = 514Keep the denominator: 27 + 37 = 57
Multiplying only the numerator: 34 = 94Multiply both numbers: 34 = 912
For 34 of 24, stopping at one part (6) or dividing by 3 (8)Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator: 24 ÷ 4 × 3 = 18
Thinking 18 is bigger than 14 because 8 is biggerA bigger denominator means more parts, so each part is smaller

faq.q: What fractions should a Year 4 child know?
faq.a: In Year 4 children find families of equivalent fractions (1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8), add and subtract fractions with the same denominator, and find fractions of amounts such as 3/4 of 24. They also start to meet tenths and hundredths as decimals.

faq.q: How do you find a fraction of an amount?
faq.a: Divide by the denominator to find one part, then multiply by the numerator. For 3/4 of 24: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, and 6 × 3 = 18.

faq.q: Why don’t you add the denominators when adding fractions?
faq.a: The denominator tells you the size of the parts, and adding does not change their size. 2/7 + 3/7 is 5 sevenths, so the answer is 5/7, not 5/14.
A fraction wall is a set of bars of the same length, each split into a different number of equal parts. Fractions that line up, such as 1/2 and 4/8, are equivalent.

12 = ?4
items.e: The bottom bar has 4 equal parts, so each half of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 1 shaded half becomes 1 × 2 = 2 shaded parts. So 12 = 24.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 12 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 12?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 12 lines up with 4 eighths, because each half is the same as 4 eighths. So 12 = 48.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 34 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 34?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 34 lines up with 6 eighths, because each quarter is the same as 2 eighths. So 34 = 68.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 23 is shaded. How many sixths are equal to 23?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 23 lines up with 4 sixths, because each third is the same as 2 sixths. So 23 = 46.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 15 is shaded. How many tenths are equal to 15?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 15 lines up with 2 tenths, because each fifth is the same as 2 tenths. So 15 = 210.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 45 is shaded. How many tenths are equal to 45?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 45 lines up with 8 tenths, because each fifth is the same as 2 tenths. So 45 = 810.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 14 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 14?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 14 lines up with 2 eighths, because each quarter is the same as 2 eighths. So 14 = 28.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Compare the shaded amounts.
items.e: Both bars are shaded up to the same place. The bottom bar has more parts, but each part is smaller, so 23 = 46.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Compare the shaded amounts.
items.e: Both bars are shaded up to the same place. The bottom bar has more parts, but each part is smaller, so 12 = 36.

items.e: 34 is the same as 6 eighths. The bottom bar has 5 shaded, so the top bar has more: 34 > 58. More parts does not mean more shaded.

items.e: Both bars are shaded up to the same place. The bottom bar has more parts, but each part is smaller, so 24 = 510.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Compare the shaded amounts.
items.e: 13 is the same as 2 sixths. The bottom bar has 3 shaded, so the bottom bar has more: 13 < 36. More parts does not mean more shaded.

items.e: 14 is the same as 2 eighths. The bottom bar has 3 shaded, so the bottom bar has more: 14 < 38. More parts does not mean more shaded.

items.e: 12 is the same as 4 eighths. The bottom bar has 3 shaded, so the top bar has more: 12 > 38. More parts does not mean more shaded.

sets.title: Equivalent fraction families and missing numbers

items.q: 34 = ?12
items.e: Look at the denominators: 4 × 3 = 12. Multiply the numerator by 3 too: 3 × 3 = 9. So 34 = 912.

items.q: 23 = ?9
items.e: Look at the denominators: 3 × 3 = 9. Multiply the numerator by 3 too: 2 × 3 = 6. So 23 = 69.

items.q: 25 = ?15
items.e: Look at the denominators: 5 × 3 = 15. Multiply the numerator by 3 too: 2 × 3 = 6. So 25 = 615.

items.q: 56 = ?12
items.e: Look at the denominators: 6 × 2 = 12. Multiply the numerator by 2 too: 5 × 2 = 10. So 56 = 1012.

items.q: 38 = ?16
items.e: Look at the denominators: 8 × 2 = 16. Multiply the numerator by 2 too: 3 × 2 = 6. So 38 = 616.

items.q: 13 = ?12
items.e: Look at the denominators: 3 × 4 = 12. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 1 × 4 = 4. So 13 = 412.

items.q: 45 = ?20
items.e: Look at the denominators: 5 × 4 = 20. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 4 × 4 = 16. So 45 = 1620.

items.q: 37 = ?14
items.e: Look at the denominators: 7 × 2 = 14. Multiply the numerator by 2 too: 3 × 2 = 6. So 37 = 614.

items.q: 23 = 8?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 2 × 4 = 8. Multiply the denominator by 4 too: 3 × 4 = 12. So 23 = 812.

items.q: 34 = 9?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 3 × 3 = 9. Multiply the denominator by 3 too: 4 × 3 = 12. So 34 = 912.

items.q: 25 = 6?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 2 × 3 = 6. Multiply the denominator by 3 too: 5 × 3 = 15. So 25 = 615.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 34?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 3 × 3 = 9 and 4 × 3 = 12. So 34 = 912. Multiplying only the numerator makes a bigger amount.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 25?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 2 × 2 = 4 and 5 × 2 = 10. So 25 = 410. Multiplying only the numerator makes a bigger amount.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 56?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 5 × 2 = 10 and 6 × 2 = 12. So 56 = 1012. Multiplying only the numerator makes a bigger amount.

items.q: Which fraction is not in the same family as 12?
items.e: 23 is not equal to 12: 1 was added to the numerator and the denominator of 12. The others are in the family, because both numbers were multiplied by the same number.

items.q: Which fraction is not in the same family as 13?
items.e: 34 is not equal to 13: 2 was added to the numerator and the denominator of 13. The others are in the family, because both numbers were multiplied by the same number.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 54 are shaded. Write this as a mixed number.
items.e: 44 = 1 whole. One more quarter is shaded. So 54 = 1 14.

items.q: 74 = ?
items.e: 44 make 1 whole. 7 − 4 = 3 quarters are left over. So 74 = 1 34.

items.q: 1 23 = ?3
items.e: 1 whole = 33. Add the 2 thirds: 3 + 2 = 5. So 1 23 = 53.

items.q: Which improper fraction is equal to 2 12?
items.e: 2 wholes = 42. Add the half: 4 + 1 = 5 halves. So 2 12 = 52.

sets.title: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator

items.q: 27 + 37 = ?
items.e: The parts are all sevenths. Count them: 2 + 3 = 5 sevenths. The denominator stays 7. So 27 + 37 = 57.

items.q: 16 + 46 = ?
items.e: The parts are all sixths. Count them: 1 + 4 = 5 sixths. The denominator stays 6. So 16 + 46 = 56.

items.q: 38 + 28 = ?
items.e: The parts are all eighths. Count them: 3 + 2 = 5 eighths. The denominator stays 8. So 38 + 28 = 58.

items.q: 412 + 512 = ?
items.e: The parts are all twelfths. Count them: 4 + 5 = 9 twelfths. The denominator stays 12. So 412 + 512 = 912.

items.q: 78 − 38 = ?
items.e: 7 eighths are shaded and 3 are crossed out. 7 − 3 = 4 eighths are left: 48.

items.q: 19 + 59 = ?
items.e: Add the numerators: 1 + 5 = 6. Keep the denominator: the parts are still ninths. So the answer is 69, not 618.

items.q: 411 + 311 = ?
items.e: Add the numerators: 4 + 3 = 7. Keep the denominator: the parts are still elevenths. So the answer is 711, not 722.

items.q: 310 + 410 = ?
items.e: Add the numerators: 3 + 4 = 7. Keep the denominator: the parts are still tenths. So the answer is 710, not 720.

items.q: 910 − 410 = ?
items.e: Subtract the numerators: 9 − 4 = 5. Keep the denominator: the parts are still tenths. So the answer is 510.

items.q: 56 − 26 = ?
items.e: Subtract the numerators: 5 − 2 = 3. Keep the denominator: the parts are still sixths. So the answer is 36.

items.q: 1112 − 712 = ?
items.e: Subtract the numerators: 11 − 7 = 4. Keep the denominator: the parts are still twelfths. So the answer is 412.

items.q: 1 − 38 = ?
items.e: 1 whole = 88. Then 88 − 38 = 58.

items.q: 1 − 25 = ?
items.e: 1 whole = 55. Then 55 − 25 = 35.

items.q: 1 − 49 = ?
items.e: 1 whole = 99. Then 99 − 49 = 59.

items.q:
35 + 45 = ?
Write the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 35 + 45 = 75. 55 make 1 whole, and 7 − 5 = 2 fifths are left over. So the answer is 1 25.

items.q:
58 + 68 = ?
Write the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 58 + 68 = 118. 88 make 1 whole, and 11 − 8 = 3 eighths are left over. So the answer is 1 38.

items.q:
23 + 23 = ?
Write the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 23 + 23 = 43. 33 make 1 whole, and 4 − 3 = 1 third is left over. So the answer is 1 13.

items.q: 29 + ?9 = 79
items.e: Think: 2 + 5 = 7. So 29 + 59 = 79.

items.q: ?10 − 310 = 410
items.e: Use the inverse: 4 + 3 = 7. So 710 − 310 = 410.

items.q: 812 − ?12 = 312
items.e: Think: 8 − 5 = 3. So 812 − 512 = 312.

items.q: Find 15 of 30.
items.e: To find 15, divide by the denominator: 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

items.q: Find 13 of 21.
items.e: To find 13, divide by the denominator: 21 ÷ 3 = 7.

items.q: Find 14 of 28.
items.e: To find 14, divide by the denominator: 28 ÷ 4 = 7.

items.q: Find 16 of 42.
items.e: To find 16, divide by the denominator: 42 ÷ 6 = 7.

items.q: Find 18 of 40.
items.e: To find 18, divide by the denominator: 40 ÷ 8 = 5.

items.q: What is 14 of 36?
items.e: To find 14, divide by the denominator: 36 ÷ 4 = 9.

items.q: What is 17 of 35?
items.e: To find 17, divide by the denominator: 35 ÷ 7 = 5.

items.q: What is 110 of 60?
items.e: To find 110, divide by the denominator: 60 ÷ 10 = 6.

items.q: What is 19 of 54?
items.e: To find 19, divide by the denominator: 54 ÷ 9 = 6.

items.q: What is 112 of 48?
items.e: To find 112, divide by the denominator: 48 ÷ 12 = 4.

items.q: Find 34 of 24.
items.e: First find 14: 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Then multiply by the numerator: 6 × 3 = 18.

items.q: Find 25 of 30.
items.e: First find 15: 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Then multiply by the numerator: 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: Find 23 of 18.
items.e: First find 13: 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Then multiply by the numerator: 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: Find 56 of 36.
items.e: First find 16: 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Then multiply by the numerator: 6 × 5 = 30.

items.q: Find 38 of 40.
items.e: First find 18: 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Then multiply by the numerator: 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: What is 25 of 35 cm?
items.e: First find 15: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 cm. Then multiply by the numerator: 7 cm × 2 = 14 cm.

items.q: What is 34 of 1,000 g?
items.e: First find 14: 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. Then multiply by the numerator: 250 g × 3 = 750 g.

items.q: What is 47 of 63?
items.e: First find 17: 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Then multiply by the numerator: 9 × 4 = 36.

items.q: What is 58 of 48?
items.e: First find 18: 48 ÷ 8 = 6. Then multiply by the numerator: 6 × 5 = 30.

items.q: What is 310 of 90 ml?
items.e: First find 110: 90 ÷ 10 = 9 ml. Then multiply by the numerator: 9 ml × 3 = 27 ml.

items.q: There are 32 pupils in a Year 4 class. 38 of them have school dinners. How many pupils have school dinners?
items.e: First find 18: 32 ÷ 8 = 4 pupils. Then multiply by the numerator: 4 pupils × 3 = 12 pupils.

items.q: Ethan has £40. He spends 25 of it on a new football. How much does the football cost?
items.e: First find 15: £40 ÷ 5 = £8. Then multiply by the numerator: £8 × 2 = £16.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Kai eats 38 of the pizza and Jack eats 28. What fraction of the pizza do they eat altogether?
items.e: The slices are all eighths. 3 + 2 = 5 eighths: 58. Keep the denominator 8.

items.q: Ava has a ribbon 60 cm long. She uses 34 of it to make a bow. How long is the piece for the bow?
items.e: First find 14: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 cm. Then multiply by the numerator: 15 cm × 3 = 45 cm.

items.q: Noah has 910 m of ribbon. He uses 410 m for a card. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 9 − 4 = 5 tenths. The denominator stays 10, so 510 m is left.

items.q: Oliver practises the piano for 34 of an hour. How many minutes is that?
items.e: There are 60 minutes in an hour (not 100). 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so 14 of an hour is 15 minutes. 15 × 3 = 45 minutes.

items.q: A book has 48 pages. Ruby has read 56 of it. How many pages does she have left to read?
items.e: 56 of 48: 48 ÷ 6 = 8, so 56 is 8 × 5 = 40 pages read. 48 − 40 = 8 pages left. (Quicker: 16 is left, and 16 of 48 is 8.)

items.q: A nature trail is 1,000 m long. Zara has walked 310 of it. How far has she walked?
items.e: First find 110: 1,000 ÷ 10 = 100 m. Then multiply by the numerator: 100 m × 3 = 300 m.

items.q: Harry has a bag of 24 sweets. 13 of them are red. How many red sweets are there?
items.e: To find 13, divide by the denominator: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 sweets.

items.q: A school car park has 60 spaces. 710 of the spaces are full. How many spaces are empty?
items.e: 710 of 60: 60 ÷ 10 = 6, and 6 × 7 = 42 spaces are full. 60 − 42 = 18 spaces are empty.

items.q: Mohammed eats 24 of a chocolate bar. Grace eats 48 of a bar of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 24 by 2: 24 = 48. Grace eats more pieces, but they are smaller, so they eat the same amount.

items.q: Leo eats 34 of a pizza. Lily eats 58 of a pizza of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: Change 34 to eighths: 34 = 68. 68 is more than 58, so Leo eats more. A bigger denominator means smaller pieces.

items.q: A jug holds 1 litre of water. Arjun pours out 310 of a litre, then 410 of a litre. What fraction of a litre is left in the jug?
items.e: He pours out 3 + 4 = 7 tenths: 710. 1 litre = 1010, and 1010 − 710 = 310 of a litre is left.

items.q: Alfie runs 58 km on Monday and 78 km on Tuesday. How far does he run altogether? Give the answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 5 + 7 = 12 eighths: 128. 88 make 1 km, and 4 eighths are left over. So he runs 1 48 km.

items.q: There are 25 pupils in a class. 35 of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school?
items.e: First find 15: 25 ÷ 5 = 5 pupils. Then multiply by the numerator: 5 pupils × 3 = 15 pupils.

items.q: A football team scored 18 goals this term. Freya scored 29 of them. How many goals did she score?
items.e: First find 19: 18 ÷ 9 = 2 goals. Then multiply by the numerator: 2 goals × 2 = 4 goals.

items.q: A packet has 20 biscuits. Charlie eats 14 of them and Aisha eats 24 of them. How many biscuits are left?
items.e: Together they eat 14 + 24 = 34, so 14 is left. 20 ÷ 4 = 5 biscuits are left.

items.q: George has £1. He spends 34 of it on sweets. How much does he spend?
items.e: £1 = 100p. 34 of 100p: 100 ÷ 4 = 25p, and 25p × 3 = 75p.

items.q: A cake is cut into 12 equal pieces. Amelia’s family eats 23 of the cake. How many pieces do they eat?
items.e: First find 13: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 pieces. Then multiply by the numerator: 4 pieces × 2 = 8 pieces.

items.q: Evie says 27 + 37 = 514. What went wrong?
c: She should add 2 to both numbers
items.e: The parts are sevenths, and they stay sevenths. Add only the numerators: 2 + 3 = 5. So 27 + 37 = 57.
